messages:
maria: Hey team — digging into an intermittent HBM thrash on prod-rtg after the client released longer seqs (many 4k/8k). Captured an nsys trace: https://perf.redwood/intern/trace/1932109876.nsys

aj: Can you paste the nsys command + what input pattern triggered it?

maria: Ran with:
```
nsys profile -o run_1932109876 --trace=cuda,osrt -w true --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none --stop-on-exit true --force-overwrite
```
Triggered with baseline load + a spike of ~120 concurrent requests with seq_len ~4096-8192.
Observations: sustained HBM bw baseline ~480 GB/s, spikes to ~880-930 GB/s during the event. KV cache read latency also spikes.

kevin: I'm seeing repeated KV eviction waves in the perfetto timeline — lots of full-page reads. Could be microbatching aligning requests to expose the same cache window. Any kernel changes around kernel selection fallback?

sasha: FYI kernel-selection change from PR #4123 added a fallback path that prefers smaller GEMM tiles for int8 on some SMs. That can increase global loads for attention kv handling. Linking PR: https://git.redwood/pr/4123

aj: Do we have top kernel timeline stats (name / duration / achieved BW)?

maria: From nsys summary (top 6):
```
triton_attention_fwd            | 12.4s | avg bw 730 GB/s
kv_page_read                    | 4.7s  | avg bw 910 GB/s
softmax_kv                      | 3.1s  | avg bw 210 GB/s
triton_gemm_small_tile          | 2.9s  | avg bw 120 GB/s
cache_eviction_handler          | 1.8s  | spike IO patterns
tensor_copy_async               | 1.1s  | host->device bursts
```
KV reads are saturating HBM during the storms (kv_page_read > 900 GB/s peaks).

perf-bot: [automated] Trace analysis -> 3 HBM saturation windows, KV read storms correlated with 2x increase in microbatch reads. Suggest instrumenting kv.cache.* metrics.

kevin: Proposed mitigation for canary: enforce request coalescing at router for seq_length >= 4096 and cap microbatch tokens to 64 per worker. Also try forcing old kernel-selection heuristic (roll back PR #4123) for the canary.

maria: I'll run the canary: disable microbatch coalescing and force old kernel selection. Re-capturing a trace now with `--trace-capture-suffix canary`.
Command: `./deploy_canary.sh --stack prod-rtg --env canary-bw-kv --force-kernel=legacy` (will run at 11:30 PST)

sasha: Also add KV cache metrics to the console: `kv.cache.evictions`, `kv.cache.prefetch_bytes`, `kv.cache.hit_rate`, `hbm.bandwidth.utilization`. Dashboards -> per-model -> add alert if eviction_rate > 0.5% per minute.

aj: Great. Once we have the canary trace, can you upload perfetto flamegraph? call out any new small-tile GEMMs that appear during spikes.

maria: Will do. I'll post perfetto links + a couple screenshot embeds in follow-up. Thanks :thumbsup:

kevin: If rollback fixes it, we need an A/B test to understand whether quality or quantization gains were worth the bandwidth cost.

maria: Agreed. Will coordinate with model-ops for AB. Creating follow-up thread for perfetto screenshots and metric graphs.
